name: FlatBuffers JSON-to-binary parsing (Parser::ParseJson)
description:
Parser::ParseJson takes a (schema-driven) Parser instance that already has a root type defined and converts an untrusted JSON text into a FlatBuffers binary buffer, by hand-recursing through the JSON grammar and encoding every scalar, string, vector, struct, table, union and nested-flatbuffer value according to the schema's FieldDef/StructDef metadata. Because it directly builds offsets, parses numeric/hex/enum constants, resolves unions "out of order" by rewinding the lexer, and supports several JSON dialects (strict vs permissive, UTF-8 vs raw, proto-style), it is a classic hand-written recursive-descent parser over attacker input and is thus a high-value fuzzing target for memory-safety and logic bugs (buffer overflows in CreateVector, incorrect union-type resolution, parse-depth stack overflows, malformed-length vectors, misaligned flexbuffers, etc.).

- Parser::ParseJson: target. Entry point; clears the internal FlatBufferBuilder, calls StartParseFile (lexer bootstrap: BOM skip, tokenization reset) then DoParseJson, which dispatches to ParseTable(root_struct_def_) — the core recursive JSON→binary encoder — and finally calls builder_.Finish()/FinishSizePrefixed().
- Parser::Parse: source. Parses a .fbs schema (or .proto in proto_mode) text that populates root_struct_def_, StructDef/EnumDef tables and IDLOptions-dependent grammar; this is normally called before ParseJson so a fuzzer can feed both a schema and subsequent JSON payloads, exercising ParseDecl/ParseEnum/ParseStruct code paths that define the types ParseTable later walks.
- Parser::Deserialize: source/variant. Loads a serialized reflection::Schema binary (as produced by Parser::Serialize or flatc -b --schema) directly into the Parser's symbol tables without re-lexing .fbs text, giving an alternate, binary-format path to set up root_struct_def_ before ParseJson — useful to fuzz ParseJson against a fixed, valid, structurally rich schema derived from untrusted bytes.
- Parser::SetRootType: config. Overrides which StructDef is used as root for parsing, directly changing which type's ParseTable call tree (and hence code paths through ParseAnyValue) is exercised.
- flatbuffers::GenText / GenerateText: consumer. Round-trips the binary buffer that ParseJson produced back into JSON text using the same Parser/schema, exercising the serialization side (PrintScalar, PrintVector, union-name lookup) and acting as a differential check that the parsed structure is self-consistent — a common idiom in the project's own tests (ParseAndGenerateTextTest, json_test.cpp).
- Parser::ParseFlexBuffer: variant. When opts.use_flexbuffers is set, JSON is parsed into a schema-less FlexBuffers builder instead of a schema-typed table, taking an entirely different encoding path (flexbuffers::Builder) that should also be exercised by varying opts.

Input space (selects different code paths inside ParseTable/ParseAnyValue/ParseVectorDelimiters/ParseTableDelimiters/SkipAnyJsonValue/ParseNestedFlatbuffer/ParseFlexBufferValue):
- The JSON text itself: object vs array roots, nested tables, vectors (fixed arrays vs growable vectors), strings with unicode/hex escapes, numeric literals (hex 0x.., inf/nan, +/- signs), enum-name vs numeric constants, "null" for non-scalar fields, unknown/extra fields, union value+type field ordering (type field appearing after or before the value, requiring lexer rewind), nested flatbuffers (field.nested_flatbuffer), flexbuffer-typed fields (field.flexbuffer), `$schema` pseudo-field.
- IDLOptions flags (set on parser.opts before Parse/ParseJson, as the existing fuzzers do): strict_json (require quoted field names), skip_unexpected_fields_in_json, allow_non_utf8 / natural_utf8, require_json_eof, size_prefixed, output_default_scalars_in_json, use_flexbuffers, proto_mode (affects schema parsing dialect).
- The accompanying schema text/binary (via Parse or Deserialize) that defines which StructDef/FieldDef/EnumDef/union layout ParseTable walks — varying it changes which branches of ParseAnyValue (scalar, struct, vector, union, string) are reached.
- Whether ParseJson is invoked once or repeatedly on the same Parser (builder_.GetSize() check rejects a second top-level JSON object), and whether root_struct_def_ is set at all (error path) — useful for exercising the API-misuse/lifecycle error branches.
